subject: Tiered uplift coverage and de-risking offer
messages:
From: Sana Malik <sana@orbitanalytics.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Lee <blee@orbitanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on SLA uplift pricing and coverage

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. Before we move to procurement, we need clarity on a couple of points around your SLA and premium support uplift:

- Can you confirm the difference in price between 99.9% and 99.95% availability? Our runbooks require a 99.95 target for the core inference routes.
- What are guaranteed P1/P2 response times for dedicated customers, and do those change with commit size?
- How does your escalation coverage work outside US business hours? We support clients globally and will need on-call handoffs for APAC incidents.
- Is there a pilot/de-risking program or short-term satisfaction SLA we can use to validate in prod before full commit?

Procurement (cc'd) will need these details for their internal approval. Can you send a short pricing worksheet and any sample contract language around credits?

Best,
Sana Malik
VP, Platform
Orbit Analytics

[Attachment: Orbit_Redwood_RFI_2027.pdf (referenced)]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Sana Malik <sana@orbitanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Lee <blee@orbitanalytics.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on SLA uplift pricing and coverage

Hi Sana — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, full worksheet attached.

- Availability bands: 99.9% (Standard) and 99.95% (Premium). Typical uplift is 18–28% on top of base hosted rates depending on commit term and model footprint. For Dedicated, the uplift is lower in absolute dollars because compute is reserved; we typically apply a 12–18% uplift for 99.95% vs 99.9% at 12‑month commit.
- Response times (Dedicated): P1 = 1 hour (oncall handoff + 15 min triage), P2 = 4 hours, P3 = 24 hours. For hosted customers with >$50k/month commit we can match these with an add-on retainer.
- Global coverage: Our standard premium plan includes a US-centric oncall rotation; for 24/7 global coverage we add an escalation retainer (flat monthly fee) that guarantees follow-the-sun handoffs with APAC overlap.
- Pilot/de-risking: we offer a 30-day pilot with a reduced commit and a satisfaction SLA: if we miss agreed-upon latency/availability baselines during the pilot window (measured via agreed dashboards), we provide a one-time credit and will extend a one-month free run at no cost.

I've attached a concise worksheet outlining price bands and a sample contract clause for credits and canary rollback windows. See attachment: Redwood_SLA_Uplift_Sheet_v2.xlsx.

Next step: if you confirm the commit bands you expect (monthly token throughput / seat counts), I can run a tailored uplift calc and a draft amendment for legal.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0198
[Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Uplift_Sheet_v2.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Ben Lee <blee@orbitanalytics.com>, Sana Malik <sana@orbitanalytics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on SLA uplift pricing and coverage

Hi Ben/Sana — looping in a quick ops note from our side on the escalation retainer and credits.

- Credit calculus: SLA credit = ((SLO_target - measured_uptime) / SLO_target) * monthly_fee * credit_multiplier (capped at 50% of the monthly fee). We can share sample calculations for your expected traffic profile.
- Canary/Rollback: Our Canary_Rollout_Playbook (attached) documents an automated rollback threshold (error rate spike >2.5x baseline OR latency >150% of baseline for 10 consecutive minutes) that triggers immediate rollback and oncall paging. That reduces blast radius and is part of the de-risking we recommend during pilot.
- Volume bands: we tier support pricing by committed monthly tokens: <100M, 100–500M, >500M. Larger commits lower the uplift percentage and reduce the retainer fee.

I'll include the playbook and a simple worked example in the spreadsheet to show the net uplift at different commit levels.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Canary_Rollout_Playbook_v1.1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Ben Lee <blee@orbitanalytics.com>

Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -07:00

Thanks — internal procurement follow-up below.

Procurement notes:
- Orbit prefers a clear, fixed monthly uplift per availability band instead of a percent-on-base model. Can you provide both formats (percent and fixed USD) in the worksheet?
- For the pilot, procurement wants a 60-day proof of concept with a rollback clause and explicit test acceptance criteria. Are you amenable to extending the pilot to 60 days if we provide a short-term reduced commit?
- We also need a sample redline for the credit cap (we usually push for a 100% cap for the pilot phase).

If you can share a revised worksheet showing fixed-dollar uplift and a 60-day pilot option, we can move to approvals next week.

Ben Lee
Head of Procurement
Orbit Analytics

[Procurement: procurement@orbitanalytics.com]

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00

Ben / Sana — thanks, updated materials attached and proposal below.

Summary of changes (attached worksheet shows line items):
- Offered both percent uplift and fixed-dollar uplift per availability tier for each commit band. Example: for 12-month commit at 100–500M tokens: 99.9% = $0 uplift (base); 99.95% = +$9,500/month (fixed) or +15% (percent) depending on preference.
- Pilot: we can extend to a 60-day pilot with a reduced commit and the same canary/rollback thresholds. For pilot only, we agree to a 100% credit cap if SLA is missed and we will provide an extra month of credits (or pro-rated refund) as remediation.
- Global oncall: added a temporary APAC overlap at no additional retainer cost for the first 3 months of the pilot to support validation. Post-pilot, follow-the-sun coverage will move to the standard escalation retainer pricing.

Next steps:
